products.short_description: Design and run M365 ↔ Google Workspace coexistence — mail routing/split delivery, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync — so both ecosystems behave as one during the transition, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Make Microsoft and Google work as one during the transition

For months during a 150k-user migration, Microsoft and Google run side by side — and users expect mail, calendars, and directory to just work across both. This solution designs and implements M365 ↔ Google Workspace coexistence: split/shared mail routing, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync, so the two ecosystems behave as one until consolidation, executed pilot-first and rollback-ready.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — the coexistence model (mail routing/split delivery, free/busy interop, directory sync) and how it bridges the transition.
  • Requirements Guide — prerequisites (both tenants + admin access, DNS/mail-flow control, directory-sync mechanism, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.
  • Implementation Guide — exact steps to configure mail routing/split delivery, cross-platform free/busy, and directory sync, validate interop on a pilot, then expand.
  • 5 supporting scripts — coexistence-readiness discovery, per-user interop validation (mail/free-busy/directory), a coexistence coverage report, safe remediation, and a scope helper.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (mail routes, free/busy resolves, directory in sync) plus Best Practices for a stable transition period.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Microsoft and Google working as one through the transition — mail routes, calendars resolve, directory stays in sync — until consolidation retires the legacy side.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • GWCOEX-Discovery.ps1 — Coexistence-readiness discovery for M365 ↔ Google Workspace
    • GWCOEX-Remediation.ps1 — Safe remediation of common coexistence gaps (default -WhatIf)
    • GWCOEX-Report.ps1 — Coexistence coverage report for M365 ↔ Google Workspace
    • GWCOEX-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — Point the coexistence scope at the pilot or all users (default -WhatIf)
    • GWCOEX-Validation.ps1 — Per-user interop validation for M365 ↔ Google coexistence

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
